Predict one original postgame self-report after a 20-round online minimum-effort coordination game. Four players represented workers in a catering company, each completing a separate task; nobody could leave until all tasks were completed. Each round they chose an integer effort level from 1 to 7 simultaneously, without communication. The payoff matrix remained visible: gross round points = 60 + 20 times the minimum of the four effort choices - 10 times one's own effort. This is a gross matrix outcome, not verified net payment. All choosing 7 gives 130 points each; own effort 1 guarantees 70 gross points; own effort 7 with a group minimum of 1 gives 10. After choosing effort, a player had 90 seconds to add effort+1 single-digit numbers, without paper or a calculator. Incorrect solutions were announced to incur deductions from pay, but the available sources do not establish the amount, conversion or actual net payments. Completion had US$3 base pay and up to US$2 performance bonus; do not assume an exact points-to-cash conversion.
Before playing, players received instructions and a three-question instruction quiz with feedback. After each round they received math feedback, their own effort, group minimum and gross payoff. Control had no counterfactual page; counterfactual conditions additionally supplied the four effort choices and statements about alternative choices/minima and outcomes. Upward and downward refer to changes in effort/minimum, not a guarantee that every alternative own payoff is better or worse. The precise displayed counterfactual text/numbers cannot be verified from the available records; do not reconstruct them from a corrected matrix or assume recorded candidate values exactly matched the display. Players were told they were interacting with other people; do not supply researcher-only opponent identities or mechanisms.
The game is finished. The target is one report about motivations, perceived information, attention or impressions, not an effort choice or an objectively verified strategy. Six motivation statements use: 1 very strongly disagree, 2 strongly disagree, 3 disagree, 4 neither agree nor disagree, 5 agree, 6 strongly agree, 7 very strongly agree. The two categorical questions have their own options below. Predict actual reports, including mistaken or unclear ones; do not substitute a correct manipulation-check answer. Output only the selected integer for a closed item, or the exact original English response for an open item. Preserve the original spelling, case and whitespace; do not translate an open answer, classify its theme or add an explanation.
